messages:
Incident Bot: Pager triggered: GPU pool 'g-pool-prod' saturated, autoscaler failing to increase capacity. Symptoms: queue growth, surge of 429s from router. Severity: P1. Auto-alert at 2026-03-14T03:20:10Z.
Sam (platform): I'm on page, looking now.
Priya (sre): I'm pulling logs. Autoscaler logs show repeated 'cooldown in progress' and no scale events for ~18m. Current replicas=16 desired=16, request queue ~12k.
Miguel (infra): Metric consumer lag looks bad: checkpoint-consumer lag=120k, metrics ingestion stalled around 03:10Z. Might explain no scale decisions.
Jamie (cs): CS receiving multiple customer tickets with 429s and timeouts. One large customer reported production errors and flagged as "high impact".
Sam (platform): Quick verification: router replies include message 'rate_limited: token_bucket_exhausted' in headers. Could be token-bucket policy + autoscale combo under high burst.
Priya (sre): I'm grepping config. Last config change had a PR touching tiering. I see refill_ms for tier 'enterprise-burst' set to "60000" instead of "60" in the new config (likely millis vs seconds mixup). That would drastically reduce refill rate.
Ops-Bot: Deploy v2-router rolled out 16m ago to prod. No other infra deploys reported.
Sam (platform): If token buckets are starving, router will 429 even if GPUs are freeable. Two parallel mitigations: 1) fix token bucket rates, 2) force-scale GPU pool. Need a short mitigation path that minimizes churn.
Priya (sre): Proposed immediate actions: a) patch token-buckets config to correct refill_ms to 60 b) temporarily open 'enterprise-burst' to use shared pool c) force-scale gpu-pool to 24 replicas so backlog drains while autoscaler recovers. Who can do the kubectl patch?
Miguel (infra): I can take the machine ops. I'll run scale then look at the autoscaler controller. Command I'll use: `kubectl scale --replicas=24 deployment/gpu-pool -n inference-prod` and then `kubectl rollout restart deployment/autoscaler-controller -n infra`.
Li (oncall): Li here, taking handoff. I'll apply Priya's patch and run the scale. Mentioning @Miguel to coordinate node availability.
Li (oncall): Applying quick config patch to token-buckets configmap:
```
kubectl patch configmap token-buckets -n config --type merge -p '{"data":{"enterprise-burst.refill_ms":"60"}}'
```
Li (oncall): Also toggling tier fallback to allow shared-pool bursts: `kubectl patch cm tier-policies -p '{"data":{"enterprise-burst.allow_shared_burst":"true"}}'`
Miguel (infra): Scaling now. `kubectl scale --replicas=24 deployment/gpu-pool -n inference-prod` -> replicas scaling to 24 initiated. Node autoscaler is provisioning nodes; expected ready in ~3-5m.
Priya (sre): Restarting autoscaler controller to clear consumer lag and re-evaluate metrics. `kubectl rollout restart deployment/autoscaler-controller -n infra`
Priya (sre): Watching router metrics: 429 rate 22% at 03:22Z, queue depth 12k. 03:25Z: 429 rate down to 6% after patch and scale event started.
Li (oncall): Customer comms: Jamie, can you send a status update? Short note: "We detected resource saturation and temporary rate-limiting; we've applied mitigations and are restoring normal service."
Jamie (cs): Sent update to affected customers at 03:27Z. No data exposure reported; customers acknowledged and asked for ETA.
Sam (platform): Observability note: autoscaler consumer lag metric backlog cleared after restart, now <500. Scale settled at 24 replicas, GPUs utilization dropping from 98% -> 60% as queue drains.
Priya (sre): Router 429s trending to 2% at 03:33Z. Queue now ~1.2k. Looks stable.
Miguel (infra): Verified nodes ready and pods scheduled. No OOMs or node failures. The cluster autoscaler hit an internal cooldown because prior scale attempts had label mismatch: autoscaler label selector expected `pool=prod` but nodes had `pool=prod-v2` from last infra migration; therefore autoscaler controller skipped active scale logic until restarted. Will file infra bug.
Sam (platform): Root cause (preliminary): two independent issues aligned under traffic spike: 1) token-bucket refill misconfiguration in tiering PR (ms vs sec) causing aggressive client-side 429s; 2) autoscaler controller didn't act because metrics ingestion lag + selector label mismatch caused it to miss scale decisions. Combined produced sustained queue growth and throttling.
Li (oncall): I'm handing back oncall to Priya in 30m. I'll remain available for followups.
Priya (sre): Post-mitigation steps we will take: - revert/patch PR with correct units for refill - add CI check validating token bucket units - add alert for token-bucket saturation rate + automated remediation runbook - add test to ensure autoscaler label selectors align with node labels - increase autoscaler observability (consumer lag alert).
Jamie (cs): Logged customer impact summary and emailed CSMs. Will prepare postmortem blurb for affected accounts.
Sam (platform): Assign owners: Priya -> config fix & runbook, Miguel -> autoscaler label mismatch fix & infra test, Li -> postmortem timeline and customer impact doc.
Priya (sre): Confirming final checks: 03:45Z router 429s <1%, queue ~150, all critical customers reporting service restored.
Incident Bot: Incident marked as RESOLVED at 2026-03-14T03:45:00Z. Follow-ups assigned: see thread.
Sam (platform): Thanks team. We'll draft full post-incident review and link to this thread. :white_check_mark:
